title: The Algorithm That Forgot the Newcomer
title_ja: 新規利用者を忘れたアルゴリズム
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Suppose a fictional community center develops a digital system for recommending activities to people who register for its programs.
sentences.ja: 架空の地域センターがプログラムに登録する人へ活動を推薦するデジタルシステムを作るとしよう。

sentences.en: The system examines previous attendance records and identifies activities that have frequently been selected by users with similar interests.
sentences.ja: 過去の参加記録を調べ似た関心の利用者がよく選んだ活動を特定する。

sentences.en: Its designers consider the recommendations successful whenever a user accepts a suggestion and subsequently attends the recommended activity.
sentences.ja: 推薦を利用者が受け入れ後に参加すると設計者は成功と考える。

sentences.en: However, a staff member becomes concerned when several recently introduced programs receive very little attention despite being prominently described in the center's printed information.
sentences.ja: しかし新設プログラムが印刷資料で目立つよう説明されてもほとんど注目されないことを職員が懸念する。

sentences.en: The designers discover that the system has relatively little information about these programs because few visitors have previously registered for them.
sentences.ja: 新しいプログラムには過去の登録者が少ないためシステムに比較的少ない情報しかないと分かる。

sentences.en: Consequently, the activities tend to appear less frequently in recommendations, which may further reduce the opportunities for visitors to discover them.
sentences.ja: その結果推薦に出にくくなり訪問者が発見する機会がさらに減る可能性がある。

sentences.en: The designers recognize that their records do not merely describe independent preferences but may partly reflect the choices that the system has already encouraged.
sentences.ja: 記録は独立した好みを示すだけでなく既にシステムが促した選択も一部反映し得ると認識する。

sentences.en: A low level of participation could indicate limited interest, limited exposure, or a combination of circumstances that the attendance figures alone cannot distinguish.
sentences.ja: 参加率の低さは関心不足、目にする機会の不足、または参加数だけでは区別できない事情の組み合わせを示し得る。

sentences.en: Rather than abandoning recommendations altogether, the team develops a hypothetical interface that separates suggestions based on previous behavior from opportunities to discover unfamiliar activities.
sentences.ja: 推薦を全面的にやめず過去行動に基づく提案と未知の活動を発見する機会を分ける仮想画面を作る。

sentences.en: A clearly labeled section displays recently introduced programs and explains that the system has not yet collected sufficient evidence to estimate their popularity.
sentences.ja: 明示した区画に新設プログラムを表示し人気を推定する十分な根拠はまだ集まっていないと説明する。

sentences.en: Users are also able to search independently instead of choosing exclusively from a list generated by the recommendation system.
sentences.ja: 推薦リストだけから選ぶのでなく自分で検索できるようにする。

sentences.en: The designers discuss whether such changes might make the interface more informative without creating an overwhelming number of options for people who simply want a quick suggestion.
sentences.ja: すぐ提案がほしい人に圧倒されるほどの選択肢を作らず、変更で画面の情報性を高められるか議論する。

sentences.en: A further question concerns the way the revised system should be evaluated if it serves several distinct purposes rather than a single objective.
sentences.ja: 修正版が単一目標でなく複数の目的を果たすならどう評価すべきかという別の問いが生じる。

sentences.en: The team proposes examining whether users can find relevant programs, whether unfamiliar activities become easier to discover, and whether the interface clearly communicates the reasons for its suggestions.
sentences.ja: 関連プログラムを見つけられるか、未知の活動を発見しやすくなるか、提案理由を明確に伝えるかを調べる案を出す。

sentences.en: They acknowledge that increased participation in a new program would not automatically establish that the recommendation system had become fairer or more useful for every participant.
sentences.ja: 新プログラムの参加増が全員にとって推薦の公平性や有用性の向上を自動的に確定しないと認める。

sentences.en: These objectives would require separate evaluation using appropriate evidence, not just a comparison of the total number of accepted recommendations.
sentences.ja: 目的ごとに適切な証拠を使う別の評価が必要で、受け入れられた推薦総数の比較だけでは足りない。

sentences.en: The fictional example illustrates how a technical system can participate in creating the patterns of behavior that its designers subsequently use to evaluate its performance.
sentences.ja: 架空の例は技術システムが後に性能評価に使う行動パターンの形成自体に関わり得ることを示す。

sentences.en: Historical records remain useful, but their significance depends partly on the conditions under which the recorded choices were made.
sentences.ja: 過去記録は有用だが意味は記録された選択が行われた条件にも依存する。

sentences.en: Responsible design requires examining the difference between a user's preferences and the opportunities that were available when those preferences were expressed through action.
sentences.ja: 責任ある設計は利用者の好みと行動でその好みが示された際に利用できた機会の違いを検討する必要がある。

sentences.en: A recommendation can be convenient without being a neutral description of what someone would have chosen if the same person had been presented with a substantially different range of possibilities.
sentences.ja: 推薦は便利でも同じ人が大幅に異なる選択肢を示された場合に選んだものの中立的記述とは限らない。

vocabulary.definition: state of being exposed to something
state of being liked by many

questions.prompt: What problem concerns the staff member?
options: All new programs are already full.
New activities receive little attention despite being advertised.
questions.explanation_ja: 新しい活動の露出不足。

questions.prompt: Why are newer programs recommended less often?
options: Users are forbidden to choose them.
They have few previous registration records.

questions.prompt: Why are historical records not independent of the system?
options: Recommendations influence the behavior that is later recorded.
Attendance is measured before any activity exists.
questions.explanation_ja: 推薦自体が記録される行動に影響。

questions.prompt: What does the revised interface offer?
options: Only a list of the most popular programs.
A compulsory registration for all activities.
A clearly labeled place to discover newer activities.
Users can consider options outside algorithmic suggestions.
The team wants to remove all recommendations.
It eliminates the need for any information.
questions.explanation_ja: 推薦以外の選択も可能。

questions.prompt: What does the team propose evaluating?
options: Multiple objectives including discoverability and clear explanations.
Only the number of accepted suggestions.
The price of the software alone.

questions.prompt: Why is increased new-program attendance insufficient?
options: It proves the system has failed.
It is unrelated to any possible goal.
It does not alone establish fairness or usefulness for everyone.
It guarantees every purpose has been achieved.
questions.explanation_ja: 参加増だけで全評価はできない。

options: Recommendations influence the choices they measure, so evaluation must consider available opportunities.
Popularity records reveal every user's true preferences.
New activities should never be recommended.
All recommendation systems are equally fair.
questions.explanation_ja: 選択機会と推薦の影響。

grammar.focus: whenever a user accepts a suggestion
which may further reduce the opportunities
grammar.explanation_ja: 非制限用法whichが前の内容を受ける。

grammar.focus: if the same person had been presented
grammar.explanation_ja: 仮定法過去完了の受動態。

paraphrases.source: Its designers consider the recommendations successful whenever a user accepts a suggestion and subsequently attends the recommended activity.
paraphrases.rewrite: The designers count a recommendation as successful each time it leads to attendance.

paraphrases.source: Consequently, the activities tend to appear less frequently in recommendations, which may further reduce the opportunities for visitors to discover them.
paraphrases.rewrite: Less frequent recommendations can further limit discovery of the new programs.

paraphrases.source: Users are also able to search independently instead of choosing exclusively from a list generated by the recommendation system.
paraphrases.rewrite: Independent search gives users an alternative to relying solely on generated suggestions.

paraphrases.source: A recommendation can be convenient without being a neutral description of what someone would have chosen if the same person had been presented with a substantially different range of possibilities.
paraphrases.rewrite: A recommendation need not reveal what a person would choose from a different set of options.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 別の選択肢での仮想判断。

discourse.role_ja: 成功指標と懸念の対比。
データ不足から露出不足へ。
記録の価値と解釈条件。
